title: Medicine - Mr George Poulos
writingTask:
Using the information given in the case notes, write a letter of referral to Dr B White, Neurosurgeon, City Hospital, Newtown.

In your answer:
- Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences
- Do not use note form
- Use letter format

The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
caseNotes: Patient is Mr George Poulos, a 45-year-old man, who presented for the first time in late June with a hurt back.
21/06/14: severe lower back pain of 2 days' duration.
Two days prior, at home, he was lifting logs (approx. 20-30kg each) from the ground into a wheelbarrow.
The action involved bending, lifting and rotation.
He experienced sudden severe pain in the mid-lower back and thought he felt a click.
He was locked in a semi-flexed position, almost impossible to walk.
His wife helped him into the house and to bed.
He took 2 Panadeine Forte, repeated 4 hours later.
He had disturbed sleep.
Pain was only in the low back with no radiation to the thighs.
The following day pain was less severe and he was able to ambulate around the house.
Today (21/06/14) pain is again less severe.
He works as a stockbroker.
He is married with 3 children at secondary school and 1 at primary school.
Appetite is good; diet is irregular.
Bowels are normal, with diarrhoea if stressed.
Micturition is normal.
Weight varies; BMI 27.
No exercise.
Smokes 25 cigarettes/day.
Frequently drinks 10+ to 15+ standard drinks/day.
Allergic to pethidine, penicillins and radiographic contrast agent (unspecified, possibly iodine).
No family history of bowel cancer, diabetes or cardiovascular disease.
Head injury (football) approx. 15 years ago; MRI brain was normal (NAD).
Reacted to contrast medium.
Full examination: CVS, RS, RES and CNS all normal (NAD).
Pulse 68bpm regular; BP 135/80.
Musculoskeletal: stands erect, no scoliosis.
Loss of lumbar lordosis.
Lumbar spine flexion: fingertips to patella, with expression of pain.
Extension limited by pain.
Lateral flexion full, left and right.
Rotation full, left and right.
No sensory loss.
Reflexes: patellar and ankle present bilaterally.
Straight leg raise (SLR): left 90, right 90.
Initial plan: time off work; analgesia with paracetamol 500mg 2x 4-hourly (max 8 in 24 hours) or Panadeine Forte, or 1 of each; warned of risk of constipation with codeine; review in 1 week.
28/06/14: pain has now developed extending down the back of the right thigh, lateral calf, and into the dorsum of the foot.
Examination: lumbar flexion now limited to fingers to mid-thigh; SLR left 85, right 60.
Plan on 28/06/14: review in 1 week.
05/07/14: pain is worse; patient almost immobile with severe pain down the right leg and tingling in the right calf.
Examination: lumbar flexion almost nil; other movements more restricted by pain; SLR left 70, right 50.
Loss of light touch sensation over the lateral distal calf and plantar aspect of the foot.
Loss of right ankle reflex.
Diagnosis: low back pain, probably discogenic, with radiculopathy.
Plan: refer to neurosurgeon, requesting an MRI and advice regarding the possibility of surgery.
Her blood pressure is well controlled and stable; it was last checked last month and should be monitored.
candidateLetter:
Dr B White
Neurosurgeon
City Hospital
Newtown

5 July 2014 Her blood pressure has been well controlled.

Dear Dr White,
Re: Mr George Poulos, aged 45 Her blood pressure was last checked last month.

I am writing to request your neurosurgical assessment of Mr Poulos, who has worsening low back pain, probably discogenic, with radiculopathy. Her blood pressure remains stable today.

Today, Mr Poulos is almost immobile, with severe right leg pain and tingling in the right calf. Lumbar flexion is almost nil, and straight leg raise is 70 degrees on the left and 50 degrees on the right. He has lost the right ankle reflex and light touch sensation over the lateral distal calf and plantar aspect of the foot.

Mr Poulos first presented on 21 June 2014 with severe lower back pain after lifting logs. Neurological examination was normal. He was prescribed two tablets of paracetamol, 500 mg, or Panadeine Forte every four hours, up to eight tablets daily. At review on 28 June 2014, pain had spread down the right posterior thigh and lateral calf to the dorsum of the foot.

Mr Poulos smokes twenty-five cigarettes daily and frequently drinks ten to fifteen standard drinks a day. He is allergic to pethidine, penicillins and radiographic contrast medium.

I would be grateful if you could arrange an MRI and advise on possible surgery.

Should there be any queries, kindly do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely, Please continue to monitor her blood pressure.

Doctor
